Issue: Tracker promotes unsupported detailed requirements as officially confirmed
Evidence: /tracker labels “01: Welcome to Leonida (Lucia Parole)” Officially Confirmed and gives $2,500 + Starter Safehouse. /missions/welcome-to-leonida instead lists $1,500 (est.). No source link substantiates either payout.
Impact: Trust, answer accuracy and retention; search loss is a risk, not measured causation
Recommended_Fix: Withdraw unsupported mission, trophy and reward claims; replace with unknown or explicitly illustrative entries. Store evidence per individual claim rather than assigning confirmation to the entire row.
Validation_Method: Review all 35 tracker records; every confirmed field must have a source and reviewer; no conflicting rewards across surfaces.

Issue: Ten published guides have no substantive guide body
Evidence: All ten sitemap /guides/{slug} URLs returned title/excerpt/related cards without a substantive guide body. Browser confirmed nightclub guide despite “21 min read”; fastest-cars guide promises “13 min read”.
Impact: Ten low-value landing pages fail stated intent; possible soft-404/quality risk
Recommended_Fix: Exclude incomplete guides from sitemap and apply noindex until substantive, reviewed content exists; derive reading time from actual body. Merge overlapping guides into stronger existing articles only where intent matches.
Validation_Method: Check every guide in initial and rendered HTML; content present, accurate reading time, self canonical, and sitemap inclusion only after quality approval.

Issue: Database confidence labels apply too broadly
Evidence: Grotti Visione says Observed in Official Media, lists 220 mph and $2,850,000 as estimates, then states CONFIRMED confidence and known street spawns. Duke Arms Carbine lists speculative attachments/drop locations alongside CONFIRMED.
Impact: Undermines the core database proposition and propagates unreliable answers
Recommended_Fix: Separate appearance identification, official name, performance, acquisition and price evidence. Remove unsupported precise numbers from reference views; retain user-entered scenarios only in clearly labelled simulators.
Validation_Method: Sample and then validate all 110 vehicles and 34 weapons; unknown values remain null; every factual field has provenance or is hidden.

Issue: Simulator warnings contradict confirmed earnings assertions
Evidence: Money calculator calls nightclub and vehicle-boosting rates CONFIRMED; FAQ asserts verified leak metadata. Business profit tool says “Verified Economic Grounding” and confirmed GTA 6 mechanics without source links.
Impact: Misleading planning results; severely weakens credibility of tools
Recommended_Fix: Remove unsupported certainty from presets, recommendations, FAQs and copied summaries. Default to editable example inputs; label output as a scenario. Temporarily noindex misleading tool pages while correcting them.
Validation_Method: Search visible text, metadata, schema and copied summaries for unsupported confirmed/verified claims; verify formulas and zero/negative boundaries.

Issue: Radio hub contradicts the site’s newer radio reporting
Evidence: /radio displays Wave 103, Flash FM, Fever 105, V-Rock and Radio Espantoso with legacy hosts and “Confirmed & Featured Tracks”. Newer /news/gta-6-radio-stations-podcasts-revealed describes a different October 8 reveal.
Impact: Two incompatible answers for one topic; readers cannot tell current facts from legacy content
Recommended_Fix: Reconcile both against the current Rockstar radio announcement. Separate historical GTA Vice City stations from GTA VI confirmations, with source/date per station and track.
Validation_Method: A reviewer can trace every GTA VI station, host and track to current evidence; both pages and previews agree.

Issue: Malformed Markdown is visible in an article heading and TOC
Evidence: Launch-trailer article visibly renders “GTA 6 [Launch Trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rz1B4B2yBZY: The Main Takeaways”. Browser screenshot and DOM confirm.
Impact: Reading and navigation quality; poor answer extraction
Recommended_Fix: Repair the stored heading and Markdown parser; render a supported, sanitized content format. Validate link syntax before publication.
Validation_Method: No raw Markdown delimiters or broken URL fragments in visible headings, TOC or accessibility tree; source link opens expected official video.

Issue: Priority article uses a 140×76 image
Evidence: Port Gellhorn OG/Twitter image is /img/apartment.jpg; direct browser image load measured 140×76. This is an actual resource measurement, not the declared OG dimensions.
Impact: Poor article hero and share quality; below Google’s large-image recommendation
Recommended_Fix: Replace with relevant, rights-cleared Port Gellhorn imagery at least 1200 pixels wide; provide accurate dimensions and a representative crop. Never upscale the tiny source as a substitute.
Validation_Method: Fetch original and optimized assets; measure intrinsic dimensions; inspect mobile crop and social preview.

Issue: Publication and author accountability are not explained
Evidence: Sample articles use Taish Team / Staff Writer and Person schema without an author URL; About describes passionate analysts but identifies no responsible editor, named owner or correction workflow.
Impact: Limits source credibility, differentiation and correction accountability
Recommended_Fix: Publish truthful ownership/editorial contact, author/team profile, sourcing policy and corrections policy. Use Organization for a real team byline, Person only for an identified human.
Validation_Method: Every article links to an authentic author/team page and correction channel; policy is reachable from article and footer.

Issue: Local production dependency audit flags critical Next.js advisory
Evidence: Local lockfile: next 15.5.24, sharp 0.35.4, source-map-js 1.2.1. npm audit --omit=dev reports 1 critical and 3 high package entries; report includes GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw. Production package versions and exploit conditions were not established.
Impact: Potential application compromise/availability risk if deployed versions and conditions match; not a proven live exploit
Recommended_Fix: First identify the deployed commit, lockfile and runtime versions. Review maintainer advisories, upgrade affected dependencies to compatible patched releases, and deploy only after staging validation. Do not run npm audit fix --force blindly.
Validation_Method: Archive production dependency manifest; relevant advisories resolved or documented as inapplicable; typecheck/build/auth/image smoke tests pass.

Issue: The workspace is not a verified copy of the live deployment
Evidence: Local robots.ts and constants.ts reference gta6atlas.com and local sitemap differs substantially from production; live robots/sitemap/JSON-LD use taishgaming.com. Numerous pre-existing local modifications.
Impact: Applying a local fix without reconciliation could regress a newer live site
Recommended_Fix: Identify the deployed repository/branch/commit and reconcile the working copy before any application edits. Keep the current user changes intact. Record deployment version in internal observability.
Validation_Method: Selected production HTML, route inventory, metadata and build revision match a reproducible checkout.

Issue: Parallel indexable database interfaces target the same entities
Evidence: /vehicles and /database/vehicles both self-canonicalize and expose the same 110-record catalog. /weapons and /database/weapons likewise overlap. This establishes overlap, not actual ranking cannibalization.
Impact: Duplicated maintenance and possible competing intent
Recommended_Fix: Choose /vehicles and /weapons as indexable hubs; bring useful filters over before permanently redirecting legacy database routes. Preserve selected/filter state when relevant.
Validation_Method: Feature parity, one hub per intent, no internal links to obsolete routes, one-hop 308s, and GSC query/page comparison after migration.

Issue: Many crawlable indexable pages are absent from the sitemap
Evidence: 107 direct 200 paths with index/follow in fetched HTML are outside the 136-entry sitemap: 92 vehicle paths (including one alias), 5 weapons, 8 locations, DMCA and one not-found article shell.
Impact: Discovery and content-governance inconsistency; absence does not itself prevent indexing
Recommended_Fix: Generate sitemap from the same approved-publication registry used by page rendering. Add only reviewed canonical records; exclude the empty/duplicate/unsupported records instead of bulk-adding all 107.
Validation_Method: For every approved canonical URL: 200, indexable, substantive, sitemap membership. No redirects/noindex/empty pages in sitemap.

Issue: Two public content paths lack incoming raw HTML links from the homepage graph
Evidence: /guides/best-weapons-tier-list and /database/weapons were not reachable in the raw-HTML anchor graph. Mobile/dropdown/JS discovery may differ; no server logs available.
Impact: Potential discoverability gap for retained content
Recommended_Fix: After consolidation, place normal anchors from the appropriate hub and relevant articles. Do not add links merely to rescue an empty guide.
Validation_Method: Retained pages reachable within three anchor clicks; verify rendered menu links as well as initial HTML.
Status: CONFIRMED RAW-HTML GRAPH / COMPLETE ORPHAN STATUS UNVERIFIED

Issue: An internally linked news URL returns HTTP 200 before rendering a not-found page
Evidence: /news/gta-6-easter-eggs-hidden-trailer-details returned 200 with index/follow and generic metadata in the fetched response. Browser subsequently displayed “404 Page Not Found”. It was discovered through a site link.
Impact: HTTP/body inconsistency and dead-end experience; Google soft-404 classification unverified
Recommended_Fix: Remove the stale internal link. Validate article existence before streaming and send a true 404 where possible; ensure the rendered not-found state is noindex. Restore only if a real article exists. Redirect only to a substantively equivalent destination.
Validation_Method: Anonymous/browser/Googlebot responses and rendered state match intended 404/noindex behavior; no internal promotion of missing article.
Status: CONFIRMED HTTP 200 / RENDERED NOT-FOUND / SOFT-404 CLASSIFICATION PROBABLE

Issue: Article template loads slowly in mobile lab run
Evidence: Port Gellhorn mobile Lighthouse: performance 64, FCP 3.1 s, LCP 4.1 s, TBT 440 ms, Speed Index 7.2 s; root-document server-response audit 1080 ms.
Impact: Delayed reading and potentially poorer engagement; real-user impact not yet measured
Recommended_Fix: Profile server reads and metadata generation; memoize shared per-request reads, cache approved public content with explicit invalidation, and isolate account/session work. Keep private responses private.
Validation_Method: Repeat comparable lab runs after changes; instrument RUM; target p75 LCP ≤2.5 s, INP ≤200 ms, CLS ≤0.1 in field data.

Issue: Homepage hydration/main-thread cost is material
Evidence: Mobile Lighthouse: TBT 701.5 ms, main-thread 4.9 s, JS execution 2.3 s. Chunk 1255-70f103200f91dd03.js accounts for about 1525 ms script evaluation in that run.
Impact: Interaction latency on slower devices; TBT is a lab proxy, not INP
Recommended_Fix: Profile the chunk with source maps in staging. Split map/dossier/secondary interactive islands, keep primary content server-rendered, and postpone below-fold nonessential code until needed.
Validation_Method: Measured main-thread reduction and lower TBT without missing text/links or broken interactions; verify INP using RUM.

Issue: Light-theme text fails measured contrast
Evidence: axe mobile homepage: 14 failing nodes in color-contrast. Examples: muted foreground #65728b on #f5f6fa 4.48:1; small #94a3b8 on white 2.56:1.
Impact: Readability and WCAG 1.4.3 barrier
Recommended_Fix: Darken muted text tokens and small labels; test real gradients/overlays in both themes. Use at least 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text.
Validation_Method: Re-run axe; manually inspect gradients, hero overlays and both color schemes; no unresolved measured contrast failures.

Issue: Five calculator controls lack accessible field names
Evidence: Money calculator spinbuttons and daily-time slider appear unnamed in the accessibility tree despite nearby visual labels. axe confirms five label-rule failures, plus 20 contrast failures on this page.
Impact: Screen-reader users cannot reliably distinguish financial inputs
Recommended_Fix: Bind each visible label with htmlFor/id or aria-labelledby; expose slider name, current value and units. Link help/errors through aria-describedby.
Validation_Method: All controls have unique accessible names; keyboard editing works; automated audit and screen-reader form navigation pass.

Issue: A homepage map pin overlaps the map CTA
Evidence: Lighthouse target-size failure: Hidden Cache #12 target partly obscured with 28×21.6 px effective space, below the 24×24 px minimum test.
Impact: Touch users may activate the wrong control
Recommended_Fix: Move the CTA outside the pin layer, enlarge hit areas, and prevent marker/control collisions on narrow screens.
Validation_Method: At 390 and 412 px widths: targets have adequate size/spacing and do not overlap; verify mouse, touch and keyboard.

Issue: Countdown labels omit parts of visible button labels
Evidence: Lighthouse flagged label-content-name-mismatch on countdown cells (e.g., “22 DAYS” accessible name versus visible date caption). Dynamic seconds also create a potential reading burden; no screen-reader timing test was performed.
Impact: Voice control and assistive-tech clarity
Recommended_Fix: Use descriptive stable control names or present the countdown as text when interaction is unnecessary. Include visible label text and describe captions without announcing every second.
Validation_Method: Re-run label-in-name checks and keyboard/voice-control tests; countdown does not spam a live region.

Issue: Character dossiers rely on JS interactions rather than durable profile pages
Evidence: /characters cards are clickable article elements and open a dialog; homepage links use /characters#jason etc. Direct #jason navigation did not open a dossier in the observed snapshot.
Impact: Deep-link/sharing friction; profile-specific search intent lacks a clear landing page
Recommended_Fix: Provide a stable, server-rendered dossier URL for each substantial profile, with normal card anchors; modal behavior can progressively enhance those links. Start with Jason/Lucia and link existing Cal/Brian stories instead of duplicating them.
Validation_Method: Direct URL, refresh, back/forward, keyboard, share links and no-JS content all work; avoid multiple competing character explainers.

Issue: Author identity and publisher logo metadata are inaccurate
Evidence: Inherited author/creator meta equals the full homepage SEO title. Article schema marks Taish Team as Person with no URL and uses /img/hero-dark.jpg as publisher logo.
Impact: Confused entity attribution and lower machine-readable quality
Recommended_Fix: Use Taish Gaming organization ID, truthful author/team IDs, and an actual logo asset. Keep branding fields independent from SEO title fields.
Validation_Method: Inspect initial and rendered metadata; JSON-LD entity references consistent; real author/team and logo URLs resolve.

Issue: Schema conveys speculative game instructions and property listings
Evidence: 11 mission details contain HowTo; six fictional property pages contain RealEstateListing. Pages are noindex, but schema still represents highly specific unsupported workflows as concrete facts.
Impact: Semantic reliability; no HowTo rich-result benefit expected
Recommended_Fix: Remove unsupported instructions first; use WebPage/CreativeWork/about relationships suitable for editorial game information. Do not model fictional fan entries as actual real-estate offers.
Validation_Method: Schema matches reviewed visible facts; parse validation plus semantic review; do not claim rich-result eligibility from type presence.

Issue: Some hubs use different OG and Twitter images
Evidence: /vehicles og:image points to /img/car-purple.jpg while twitter:image uses /img/hero-dark.jpg. Vehicles original is 800×436 although OG declares 1200×630.
Impact: Inconsistent and under-sized social previews
Recommended_Fix: Generate OG/Twitter images from one per-page image record with actual dimensions; use relevant large source assets.
Validation_Method: Preview metadata URLs agree where intended and fetched image dimensions match declarations.

Issue: Large-image preview permission is absent in sampled meta/header directives
Evidence: None of the 277 normalized paths has max-image-preview:large in parsed robots metadata; sampled response headers also lacked this directive. Existing content is not thereby ineligible for Discover.
Impact: Missed control supporting large image presentation
Recommended_Fix: Add max-image-preview:large for approved public editorial pages and supply relevant large images. Preserve noindex on incomplete/private pages.
Validation_Method: Googlebot receives correct directive and large reachable article image; GSC impressions monitored without guaranteed outcomes.

Issue: Live CSP only controls embedding
Evidence: Content-Security-Policy is exactly frame-ancestors none (quoted in response); no script-src, object-src, base-uri or default-src restrictions. HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options are already present.
Impact: Defense-in-depth gap; does not prove an XSS vulnerability
Recommended_Fix: Build a nonce/hash-compatible CSP in staging, deploy Report-Only first, collect violations, then enforce tested directives. Allow only required image/video/connect origins.
Validation_Method: No blocked legitimate scripts/auth/embeds; no unsafe broad policy changes; CSP reporting and enforcement confirmed.

Issue: Privacy text does not fully explain visible account/newsletter features
Evidence: Privacy page mentions local storage, logs and contact inquiries, but not an explicit newsletter-processing/retention/unsubscribe account; login and newsletter interfaces are present. It states local progress never leaves the device unless exported, while login advertises saved account progress.
Impact: User expectations and possible legal-review gap; no legal breach concluded
Recommended_Fix: Trace real data flows, recipients, retention, deletion, exports and email subscription lifecycle; update policy to actual behavior. Only show consent controls when the actual services/jurisdictions require them.
Validation_Method: Policy compared with observed network/storage behavior and backend configuration; legal specialist reviews relevant jurisdictional obligations.

Issue: Homepage capture copy says existing tools have not launched
Evidence: Hero signup says be first to know when weapons database, interactive map and money calculator go live, while all three are accessible. Countdown/calendar text also still mentions GTA 6 Atlas.
Impact: Confusing readiness and weak signup proposition
Recommended_Fix: Rewrite signup around factual update benefits; use current Taish Gaming brand in calendar/share text; put primary product entry points before the signup ask.
Validation_Method: Signup copy matches available features; mobile first view communicates purpose and useful next action; evaluate CTA usage and confirmed subscription rate.

Issue: Vehicle database counts and categories disagree
Evidence: /database/vehicles reports 110/110, All Vehicles 312, Recently Viewed 6 in a fresh session, Cars 1 and Trucks/SUVs 0 while many car/truck/SUV entries are listed.
Impact: Filtering credibility and catalog usability
Recommended_Fix: Derive counters, category mappings and history from the same current dataset/session; remove fabricated/default totals and provide empty states.
Validation_Method: Counters equal actual filter results; fresh session has no invented browsing history; category totals reconcile.

Issue: Local type checking fails in three locations
Evidence: tsc reports TS2322 at dashboard-view.tsx:104 and weapons-client.tsx:236,244. Lint completed with warnings and no reported errors.
Impact: Blocks reliable release validation for this checkout; does not prove production build failure
Recommended_Fix: Fix nullable numeric props and string/number normalization in the correct production-aligned branch; retain explicit unknown states.
Validation_Method: npm run typecheck and production build succeed; unknown values render as unknown rather than zero.

Issue: Related cards can repeat stronger claims than cautious article body
Evidence: Port Gellhorn article correctly says exact official map boundaries are unreleased, while related cards claim specific map-size multiples with “Rockstar says” language. Full source trail for those card assertions is not provided at the point of claim.
Impact: Promotional summaries may overstate underlying evidence
Recommended_Fix: Fact-check title, excerpt, sidebar, card, social text and article body together; attribute any exact size claim to an identifiable current source.
Validation_Method: One approved claim record generates all summaries; citation review confirms wording and scope.
Status: CONFIRMED CROSS-SURFACE CLAIM / FACTUAL ACCURACY REQUIRES SOURCE REVIEW

Issue: Favicon returns 404 in Lighthouse
Evidence: Both mobile Lighthouse runs log /favicon.ico as a 404; no other failed application resource was established by those reports.
Impact: Browser polish and console noise
Recommended_Fix: Add correct favicon/app icons in the production app and verify route and MIME type.
Validation_Method: Direct favicon URL returns a valid icon with 200; fresh-browser console no longer records this error.

Issue: Growth attribution and crawl diagnosis require private data
Evidence: No GSC, GA4, Bing Webmaster, rank-tracking exports, backlink index or verified bot logs were supplied. No GA4/GTM request was observed in the initial homepage resource sample; this does not prove analytics is absent.
Impact: Cannot prioritize by actual traffic, evaluate cannibalization or confirm crawl/indexation
Recommended_Fix: Establish a baseline from owner-accessible tools, add privacy-appropriate events/RUM, and document content cohorts. Request exports through normal authorized access.
Validation_Method: Baseline dashboard shows source/page/query trends and real-user vitals; no invented traffic or backlink metrics.

Issue: Mobile article TOC delays the substantive answer
Evidence: Launch-trailer mobile screenshot shows the hero then an 18-entry TOC; actual article answer begins after the long list. The malformed first TOC item further increases vertical space.
Impact: Reading friction for search and assistant referrals
Recommended_Fix: Put a short sourced answer directly below the byline; collapse the TOC on mobile with an accessible disclosure. Keep section navigation available.
Validation_Method: At 390×844 users see topic, short answer/evidence and next step early; test expand/collapse, keyboard and jump targets.
